name: Brainspace
desc: Developed AI-driven analytics software that helps legal and investigation teams review large document sets in e-discovery.
markets: Legal, compliance and government customers, mainly in the United States; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Niche legal-technology software brand with no consumer profile; little brand-marketing need, so F1 hospitality is the only angle.
changed: Acquired by Cyxtera in 2019

name: GE Aerospace
desc: Designs and makes jet engines, avionics and related systems, and services them for airlines, aircraft makers and militaries.
markets: Engines and services for airlines, airframers and militaries worldwide, including CFM LEAP engines built with Safran.
rationale: Global aviation supplier with an engineering and technology story and B2B hospitality value with airlines and airframers; consumer marketing is limited.
changed: Renamed GE Aerospace in 2024 after the GE spin-offs

name: SatixFy
desc: Designs satellite communication chips and digital beamforming antennas for satellite terminals used in aviation, defence and mobile services.
markets: Satellite operators and terminal makers; Israeli base with listing in the United States; international customers likely but not confirmed.
rationale: B2B chip designer with technology showcase value but no consumer brand and a small marketing budget; weak F1 fit.
changed: Takeover by MDA Space agreed in 2025

name: UrtheCast
desc: Operated cameras on the International Space Station and sold satellite imagery, video and analytics to governments and agriculture customers.
markets: Satellite imagery for government and commercial customers; Canadian base; no current operations known.
rationale: Earth observation company that ran into financial difficulty; no active marketing, so very unlikely F1 prospect.
changed: Entered insolvency proceedings around 2020 and assets were sold

name: NanoRacks
desc: Provided commercial services on the International Space Station, launching small satellites and hosting customer experiments for research and commercial clients.
markets: Customers included space agencies, universities and companies from several countries using ISS research and satellite deployment services.
rationale: Space services brand now inside Voyager; technology storytelling possible but little consumer marketing, so modest F1 fit.
changed: Acquired by Voyager Space in 2021

name: Avenger Flight Group
desc: Florida company listed under aerospace and air transport, described as a provider of commercial aviation services.
markets: Florida-based aviation services; customers and geography not confirmed.
rationale: Small aviation services company with unclear offering and little marketing profile; weak F1 fit.

name: Ovzon
desc: Provides satellite broadband connectivity for military, government and security customers through the Ovzon 3 geostationary satellite.
markets: Mobile satellite broadband for defence and security customers worldwide; Swedish base; no consumer business.
rationale: Defence-focused satellite operator with no consumer profile and small marketing budget; weak F1 fit.

name: OfficeSpace Software
desc: Sells cloud workplace management and desk booking software that helps corporations and universities manage floor plans and occupancy.
markets: Corporate and university facilities teams, mainly in the United States; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Mid-size SaaS vendor with enterprise customers; F1 hospitality could suit client entertainment, but brand reach is small.

name: Hanwha Systems
desc: Makes defence electronics such as radars, command systems, sensors and satellite equipment, and provides IT services and smart city systems.
markets: South Korean defence electronics and ICT group member; exports to defence customers abroad and satellite activities.
rationale: Defence-led electronics firm with a Korean group brand; technology showcase possible but weapons focus limits fit.

name: Procket Networks
desc: Developed high-performance carrier-class routers for telecom service providers before being absorbed into Cisco.
markets: Core routers sold to telecom carriers; absorbed into Cisco's routing business and no longer operates independently.
rationale: No longer an independent brand, so no marketing rationale for an F1 partnership.
changed: Acquired by Cisco Systems in 2004
f1: Parent Cisco (Webex) is a current Formula 1 partner; Procket itself no longer exists

name: Woodward
desc: Designs and makes fuel systems, engine controls, actuation and electric power systems for aircraft and industrial engines.
markets: Supplies aerospace OEMs and industrial customers across North America, Europe and Asia; customers include Boeing, Airbus and GE.
rationale: Engineering-led B2B supplier with motorsport-adjacent controls technology; limited consumer marketing but possible B2B hospitality value.

name: TCR
desc: Supplies and services airport ground support equipment such as baggage tractors, loaders and ground power units through leasing and maintenance.
markets: Airports and ground handlers across Europe, with Belgian base; wider expansion not confirmed.
rationale: B2B ground equipment lessor; trackside hospitality could help airport and airline clients, but brand marketing is limited.

name: Spaceflight Industries
desc: Former small-satellite launch broker that also owned the BlackSky Earth imaging business and later renamed itself BlackSky Holdings.
markets: Launch services for satellite makers and governments; the name was later replaced by BlackSky.
rationale: Name no longer in use as a brand; the surviving imaging business is B2B and government focused.
changed: Renamed BlackSky Holdings in 2019

name: 3D Robotics
desc: Makes professional drones and software for mapping, surveying and inspection, including the Site Scan platform used with Esri.
markets: Enterprise and construction customers, mainly in the United States; shifted from consumer drones to software.
rationale: Small enterprise drone software brand; technology showcase possible but limited budget and consumer reach.

name: TTTech
desc: Develops safe networked computing platforms for aerospace, automotive and industrial markets, including time-triggered Ethernet technology.
markets: Customers in aerospace, automotive and industrial sectors across Europe, North America and Asia, including major carmakers and aerospace firms.
rationale: Deep-tech supplier of safety-critical networking; technology tie-in with motorsport and automotive but little consumer brand marketing.

name: CDI
desc: Provides engineering and IT staffing and technical services to industrial, aerospace and energy customers in several countries.
markets: Offices in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada and the Middle East serving industrial, aerospace and energy clients.
rationale: B2B staffing firm with engineering niche; F1 could support recruitment branding and client hospitality, but marketing appetite is modest.
changed: Acquired by AE Industrial Partners in 2017

name: Air Transport Services Group
desc: Leases freighter aircraft and provides air cargo transportation and aircraft maintenance services to carriers and delivery companies.
markets: Cargo airline and leasing customers include major e-commerce and express carriers; mainly United States based.
rationale: B2B air cargo lessor; F1 freight logistics ties exist elsewhere but this firm has little brand marketing.
changed: Taken private by Stonepeak in 2025

name: Forever OSS
desc: Chinese information technology company linked to aerospace and mobile enterprise software; products and customers are not confirmed.
markets: Appears to serve Chinese organisations; no international activity confirmed.
rationale: Unclear B2B software business with little known marketing profile; weak F1 fit.

name: Adam Aircraft
desc: Developed the A500 twin-engine piston aircraft and A700 very light jet, but ceased operating after financial difficulty.
markets: Sold light aircraft mainly to US customers; collapsed financially around 2008.
rationale: Defunct aircraft maker with no marketing activity; not a viable F1 prospect.
changed: Filed for bankruptcy in 2008

name: DiGiFi Korea
desc: South Korean satellite communications and IT company providing maritime and remote-area connectivity services to shipping and energy customers.
markets: Describes itself as a global satellite communication company; customers include shipping fleets and remote-area enterprises.
rationale: B2B satellite connectivity provider with little consumer brand; F1 could help maritime industry networking but fit is weak.

name: Killick Aerospace
desc: Supplies commercial aircraft and engine parts and offers leasing, trading and professional aerospace services to airlines and lessors.
markets: Airlines, lessors and maintenance providers worldwide buy parts, leases and services.
rationale: B2B aircraft parts trader with no consumer profile; F1 hospitality might help client relations but fit is weak.

name: Northstar Aerospace
desc: Made helicopter and aircraft transmission components, gears and drive systems before entering creditor protection and being broken up.
markets: Plants in Canada, the United States and the United Kingdom supplied helicopter makers until the company failed in 2012.
rationale: Defunct component maker with no brand to market; not an F1 prospect.
changed: Entered creditor protection in 2012 and operations were sold

name: XO
desc: Sells private jet charter, jet cards and memberships on a marketplace of operators, plus a fleet of its own jets.
markets: Customers are US-based flyers; part of the Vista group, which also runs VistaJet internationally.
rationale: Premium private aviation brand under the group that owns VistaJet, a current F1 partner; wealthy-client hospitality fits well.
changed: Acquired by Vista Global in 2020
f1: Sister brand VistaJet, owned by the same parent Vista Global, is a current Formula 1 partner

name: Mesa Air Group
desc: Operates regional airline flights under capacity purchase agreements for major carriers such as American Airlines and United.
markets: Flies regional routes within North America on behalf of major US airlines.
rationale: Contract regional carrier with no consumer brand of its own; weak F1 fit.
changed: Merger with Republic Airways agreed in 2025

name: Autonomous Control Systems Laboratory
desc: Develops industrial drones and flight control software for inspection, logistics, surveying and security, mainly for Japanese customers.
markets: Customers are Japanese utilities, government bodies and companies; no confirmed overseas expansion.
rationale: Japanese industrial drone maker with niche B2B profile; technology showcase possible but limited marketing and domestic focus.

name: Avanti Communications
desc: Operates Ka-band satellite broadband capacity across Europe, the Middle East and Africa for telecom operators, governments and enterprises.
markets: Sells satellite capacity in Europe, the Middle East and Africa to operators, governments and broadcasters.
rationale: B2B satellite capacity seller with no consumer awareness; limited budget and marketing need.
changed: Creditors took control in a 2017 debt restructuring and shares were delisted

name: Héroux-Devtek
desc: Makes aircraft landing gear and aerostructures for fighter, transport and commercial aircraft programmes.
markets: Landing gear and structures supplied to aircraft makers and defence customers in Canada, the United States and Europe.
rationale: Precision aerospace supplier with no consumer brand; modest F1 relevance via engineering and hospitality.
changed: Taken private by Platinum Equity in 2024

name: ProtoStar
desc: Bought and launched a geostationary satellite to lease capacity to broadcasters and data customers in Asia before going bankrupt.
markets: Leased capacity from one satellite to Asian broadcasters and data customers until bankruptcy in 2009.
rationale: Defunct satellite operator that went bankrupt in 2009 and has no marketing activity; not an F1 prospect.
changed: Filed for bankruptcy in 2009 and assets were sold to Intelsat

name: Kaman
desc: Makes aerostructures, fuzing, bearings and power transmission products and the K-MAX helicopter for defence, aerospace and industrial customers.
markets: Supplies Boeing, Airbus, US defence and industrial manufacturers, mainly from North American operations.
rationale: B2B engineering supplier with no consumer profile; limited marketing need and defence exposure.
changed: Acquired by Arcline Investment Management in 2024

name: General Dynamics
desc: Builds Gulfstream business jets, combat vehicles, submarines and defence electronics and IT services for governments and corporate customers.
markets: Operates worldwide through Gulfstream, marine systems, combat systems and technologies units serving governments and business jet buyers.
rationale: Gulfstream business jets suit F1 hospitality and wealthy buyers, but defence core limits brand fit.

name: MTAR Technologies
desc: Makes precision components for space launch vehicles, nuclear power, defence, aerospace and clean energy, including Bloom Energy fuel cell parts.
markets: Indian state agencies such as ISRO plus global clean energy and aerospace manufacturers, notably Bloom Energy in the United States.
rationale: B2B precision manufacturer with minimal consumer visibility; engineering story fits F1 technology, but marketing budget is small.

name: KEYW Corporation
desc: Provided cybersecurity, cyber operations, signals intelligence and analytics services to the US intelligence community and defence department.
markets: US government customers only; the company was absorbed into Jacobs and no longer trades.
rationale: Absorbed into Jacobs, so no standalone brand to market; no F1 rationale.
changed: Acquired by Jacobs Engineering in 2019

name: Internet Gold - Golden Lines
desc: Israeli telecommunications holding company that controlled Internet Gold and Golden Lines and held stakes in Bezeq through B Communications.
markets: Israeli internet and telecom services; holding structure tied to the Eurocom group with no overseas operations known.
rationale: Holding structure with little brand visibility and no international activity; weak F1 fit.

name: Wheels Up
desc: Sells private jet memberships, charter flights and aircraft management using its own and partner fleets, mainly in North America.
markets: Wealthy individuals and corporate flyers in the United States; no verified expansion beyond North America.
rationale: Private aviation brand whose rivals Flexjet and VistaJet already sponsor F1; premium client hospitality fits well.

name: Hainan Airlines
desc: Full-service Chinese airline founded in 1993, based on Hainan island and flying domestic and international routes.
markets: Domestic Chinese network plus international routes to Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific; part of the Hainan Airlines group.
rationale: Large Chinese airline whose rivals Qatar Airways and Singapore Airlines sponsor F1; useful for Chinese Grand Prix marketing and premium travellers.

name: Alaska Airlines
desc: Major US airline flying passengers and cargo from hubs including Seattle and Portland, expanded by its merger with Hawaiian Airlines.
markets: US network plus Canada, Mexico and Latin America; the Hawaiian merger added trans-Pacific routes to Asia and Oceania.
rationale: Large US carrier with consumer brand and premium cabin offers; rivals sponsor F1 but fit is mostly US-centred.
changed: Acquired Hawaiian Airlines in 2024

name: American Airlines
desc: Operates a large global passenger airline network with hubs including Dallas-Fort Worth, Charlotte and Chicago, flying to hundreds of destinations.
markets: Flies across North America, Latin America, Europe and Asia-Pacific, with oneworld alliance partners and a big US domestic network.
rationale: Global brand-led airline with premium corporate travellers and US Grand Prix relevance; rivals already sponsor F1.

name: Southwest Airlines
desc: Operates a low-cost Boeing 737 passenger airline, the largest US domestic carrier by passengers, serving North America and nearby regions.
markets: US domestic network plus Mexico, Caribbean and Central America destinations; no transatlantic or Asian service.
rationale: Large consumer brand focused on the US; F1 could support US Grand Prix marketing but international appeal is limited.

name: United Airlines
desc: Operates a major US passenger and cargo airline with hubs in Chicago, Newark, Houston, Denver, San Francisco and Washington.
markets: Flies to hundreds of destinations across North America, Latin America, Europe and Asia-Pacific as a Star Alliance member.
rationale: Global consumer airline with premium corporate travellers and US Grand Prix relevance; rival carriers sponsor F1.

name: International Airlines Group
desc: Owns British Airways, Iberia, Vueling, Aer Lingus, Level and the Avios loyalty scheme, flying a large European and transatlantic network.
markets: British Airways, Iberia, Aer Lingus and Vueling serve Europe, North America, Latin America, Africa and Asia.
rationale: Global airline group with strong brands and premium travellers; British Airways and rivals suit F1 hospitality.

name: NEOM
desc: Saudi giga-project developing planned cities, ports, resorts and industrial zones including The Line, Oxagon, Trojena and Sindalah.
markets: Saudi-based developments seeking global tourism, investment and residents; owned by the Public Investment Fund and heavily active in sport sponsorship.
rationale: Destination and investment brand already active in global sport; F1 offers worldwide exposure and B2B hospitality, though project delivery is uncertain.

name: Sumisho Air Lease
desc: Buys commercial aircraft and leases them to airlines; subsidiary of Sumitomo Corporation with a US office in Los Angeles.
markets: Leases aircraft to airlines worldwide as part of Sumitomo Corporation; no consumer business.
rationale: B2B aircraft lessor with no consumer brand and little marketing need; hospitality value is limited.

name: Surf Air Mobility
desc: Provides regional air mobility through Surf Air membership flights and Southern Airways Express, and develops electric aircraft powertrains.
markets: Subscription and per-flight regional flying between US airports using Cessna Caravan aircraft.
rationale: Premium regional flying brand with electrification story; F1 sustainability angle exists but audience is mostly US.

name: AerCap
desc: World's largest aircraft lessor, owning and managing aircraft, engines and helicopters leased to airlines around the world.
markets: Leases aircraft and engines to airlines across Europe, Americas, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and Africa.
rationale: Global B2B lessor with airline clients; F1 hospitality fits client entertainment, but there is no consumer marketing.

name: LATAM Airlines Group
desc: Latin America's largest airline group, with passenger and cargo operations through affiliates in Chile, Brazil, Peru, Colombia and Ecuador.
markets: Network across Latin America plus flights to North America, Europe and Oceania.
rationale: Largest Latin American airline with Brazilian and Mexican Grand Prix relevance; rivals sponsor F1.

name: Vietjet
desc: Vietnamese low-cost airline flying domestic and international routes across Asia, founded by Nguyen Thi Phuong Thao.
markets: Domestic Vietnam network plus routes across Asia and to Australia and India.
rationale: Brand-led budget airline with strong consumer marketing in Asia; F1 gives regional exposure for an expanding carrier.

name: DSV
desc: Provides global air, sea and road freight forwarding and contract logistics services to business customers.
markets: Offices in about 80 countries serving shippers in Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and Africa.
rationale: Global logistics rival of F1 partners DHL and CEVA; strong B2B hospitality value with freight customers.
changed: Acquired DB Schenker in 2025

name: Heathrow Airport Holdings
desc: Owns and operates London Heathrow, Britain's busiest airport, earning revenue from airline charges, retail, parking and property.
markets: Serves airlines flying to destinations across Europe, the Americas, Asia, Africa and the Middle East, with tens of millions of passengers.
rationale: Major airport brand with premium passengers and British Grand Prix links; sponsorship value lies in hospitality and retail partners.

name: Vietnam Airlines
desc: Vietnam's flag carrier, flying Airbus and Boeing aircraft on domestic and international routes across Asia, Europe, Oceania and North America.
markets: Network across Vietnam, Asia, Europe, Australia and the United States, with majority state ownership.
rationale: Flag carrier with national marketing role; rivals sponsor F1, though Vietnam hosts no Grand Prix currently.

name: Bangalore International Airport Limited
desc: Operates Kempegowda International Airport in Bengaluru, India's third busiest airport, handling tens of millions of passengers a year.
markets: One Indian airport serving domestic and international airlines and passengers.
rationale: Single-airport operator with domestic focus; limited marketing need and weak F1 fit.

name: gategroup
desc: Supplies airline catering, onboard retail products, equipment and lounges to airlines through units in about 60 countries.
markets: Operates over 190 units in about 60 countries serving airlines worldwide.
rationale: B2B airline caterer with no consumer brand; hospitality and product showcase possible, but marketing appetite is small.

name: Gol Linhas Aéreas
desc: Brazilian low-cost airline flying Boeing 737 jets on domestic routes and to destinations in South America and the Caribbean.
markets: Brazil domestic network plus South America and some Caribbean and US destinations.
rationale: Large Brazilian consumer airline with São Paulo Grand Prix relevance; rivals sponsor F1, but its finances are recovering.
changed: Filed Chapter 11 in 2024 and emerged in 2025

name: Virgin Atlantic
desc: British long-haul airline flying from Heathrow, Gatwick and Manchester to North America, the Caribbean, Africa, the Middle East and Asia.
markets: Transatlantic core network plus Caribbean, Africa, India and Asia routes, in partnership with Delta.
rationale: Brand-led premium British airline with transatlantic travellers and British Grand Prix relevance; peers already sponsor F1.

name: Grupo Aeroméxico
desc: Mexico's flag-carrier airline group flying domestic routes and international routes to the United States, Latin America, Europe and Asia.
markets: Mexican network plus flights to the US, Latin America, Europe and Asia; SkyTeam member.
rationale: Mexican flag carrier with Mexico City Grand Prix link; rivals sponsor F1 and consumer reach is large.

name: JetBlue Airways
desc: Passenger airline founded in 1998, flying from New York JFK, Boston and Fort Lauderdale across the US, Caribbean and Europe.
markets: US domestic network plus Caribbean, Latin America and transatlantic routes to London, Paris and Amsterdam.
rationale: Consumer-facing US carrier with New York and Miami exposure; F1 gives US Grand Prix and premium cabin marketing.

name: Delta Air Lines
desc: Major US airline operating a hub-and-spoke network to more than 275 destinations, with large international and premium cabin operations.
markets: Flies across North America, Latin America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Africa, with SkyTeam and joint-venture partners.
rationale: Premium-heavy global carrier with corporate clients; rivals already sponsor F1 and US races give strong exposure.

name: Garuda Indonesia
desc: Indonesia's national flag carrier, flying domestic and international routes from Jakarta across Asia, Australia, the Middle East and Europe.
markets: Domestic Indonesian network plus international routes in Asia, Oceania and the Middle East; majority state-owned.
rationale: National carrier with brand ambitions in Asia; F1 could support recovery marketing though finances have been weak.

name: Ryanair
desc: Europe's largest low-cost airline group, flying Boeing 737 aircraft to hundreds of airports across Europe and neighbouring countries.
markets: Network of airports across Europe plus Morocco, Jordan and other neighbouring countries.
rationale: Huge consumer airline in Europe with price-led marketing; F1 audience overlaps but brand style is not premium.

name: Azerbaijan Airlines
desc: State-owned flag carrier of Azerbaijan flying Airbus, Boeing and Embraer aircraft to destinations in Europe, Asia and the Middle East.
markets: Baku-based network of routes in Europe, Asia and the Middle East; owned by the Azerbaijani state.
rationale: Flag carrier based in a Grand Prix host city; national branding value, though it faced setbacks after a 2024 crash.

name: Spirit Airlines
desc: Ultra-low-cost US airline flying Airbus A320-family aircraft across the United States, Caribbean and Latin America with unbundled fares.
markets: US network plus Caribbean and Latin America destinations on a budget model.
rationale: Budget carrier in restructuring with little premium positioning; weak F1 fit despite Miami Grand Prix proximity.
changed: Filed for Chapter 11 in 2024 and again in 2025

name: Fraport Greece
desc: Operates 14 regional Greek airports, including Thessaloniki, Mykonos, Santorini, Corfu and Rhodes, under a 40-year concession.
markets: Fourteen Greek airports serving mainly European holiday traffic; owned by Fraport AG and a Greek partner.
rationale: Airport operator with tourism marketing needs; Greek island brand exposure is niche and there is no Greek Grand Prix.

name: Mundys
desc: Italian infrastructure group that owns and operates toll roads and airports, including Abertis, Aeroporti di Roma and Telepass.
industry: toll road and airport infrastructure group
markets: Operates toll roads and airports in Italy, Spain, France, Latin America and the United States.
rationale: Mobility infrastructure group with Italian visibility and corporate hospitality needs; Italian Grand Prix link, but little consumer marketing.
changed: Renamed from Atlantia to Mundys in 2023

name: ixigo
desc: Indian online travel app for train, flight, bus and hotel bookings, strongest in rail ticketing with live train tools.
markets: Mass-market Indian travellers; no verified expansion outside India.
rationale: Consumer travel app with Indian reach; F1 audience is growing in India but its mass-market focus makes fit weak.

name: ITA Airways
desc: Italian flag carrier created in 2021 as successor to Alitalia, flying to Europe, the Americas, Africa and Asia from Rome.
markets: Rome hub network to Europe, North and South America, Africa and Asia; Lufthansa Group holds a minority stake.
rationale: Italian carrier with strong national brand and Italian Grand Prix link; rival flag carriers already sponsor F1.
parent: Italian Ministry of Economy and Finance
changed: Created in 2021 as successor to Alitalia

name: Riyadh Air
desc: New Saudi flag carrier launched in 2023 and owned by the Public Investment Fund, aiming at premium international travel.
markets: Early-stage network from Riyadh; planned long-haul expansion with aircraft orders, but current network is limited.
rationale: Young state-backed Saudi carrier building its brand globally; Saudi Grand Prix and Gulf peers sponsoring F1 make a strong fit.
changed: Launched in 2023

name: Mumbai International Airport
desc: Operates Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport in Mumbai, earning from airline charges, retail and property.
markets: One Mumbai airport serving domestic and international airlines; controlled by Adani Airport Holdings.
rationale: Single airport operator with local focus; limited marketing need and weak F1 fit.

name: China Eastern Airlines
desc: Shanghai-based flag carrier and one of China's three largest airlines, flying domestic and international routes as a SkyTeam member.
markets: Domestic Chinese network plus routes to Asia, Europe, North America and Oceania; state-controlled.
rationale: Large Chinese carrier whose home Shanghai hosts the Chinese Grand Prix; rival carriers already sponsor F1.

name: HALO AirFinance
desc: Joint venture of Tokyo Century and Carlyle Aviation Partners providing aircraft financing to commercial airlines and lessors.
markets: Finances airlines and lessors; owners based in Japan and the United States.
rationale: B2B aircraft financier with no consumer brand; owner Carlyle is already an F1 partner, so hospitality value is real.
parent: Tokyo Century and Carlyle Aviation Partners (joint venture)
f1: Co-owner Carlyle (through Carlyle Aviation Partners) is a current Formula 1 global partner

name: Reliable Robotics
desc: Develops automated flight systems that let cargo aircraft such as the Cessna Caravan fly with remote pilots under FAA oversight.
markets: Works with the FAA and US cargo operators; no confirmed commercial operations abroad.
rationale: Early-stage aviation automation developer with technology storytelling but little brand budget; weak F1 fit.

name: Ethiopian Airlines
desc: State-owned flag carrier and Africa's largest airline, flying from its Addis Ababa hub to more than 140 destinations worldwide.
markets: African hub network linking Africa with Europe, Asia, the Middle East and the Americas.
rationale: Large African airline with brand ambitions and growing international network; F1 gives global exposure but spend is cautious.

name: Virgin Australia
desc: Australia's second-largest airline, flying domestic routes and some international routes from Brisbane and other Australian cities.
markets: Australian domestic network plus routes to New Zealand, Fiji, Bali and other nearby destinations.
rationale: Australian consumer airline with Melbourne Grand Prix relevance; fit is good but its international reach is narrow.
changed: Entered administration in 2020, bought by Bain Capital, and relisted in 2025

name: Aegean Airlines
desc: Greece's largest airline, flying scheduled and charter routes across Europe and the Middle East from Athens, a Star Alliance member.
markets: Greek domestic and European network plus Middle East destinations.
rationale: Regional carrier with strong Greek brand; F1 fit is modest because its audience is mostly Greek and European.

name: Beond
desc: Dubai-based premium leisure airline, founded in the Maldives and Dubai, flying business-class style services to leisure destinations.
markets: Premium flights linking Dubai and Europe with the Maldives and other leisure destinations; network is small.
rationale: Gulf premium-leisure start-up whose wealthy audience suits F1 hospitality; Abu Dhabi Grand Prix proximity helps.

name: Willis Mitsui & Co. Engine Support
desc: Leases aircraft engines through a joint venture of Willis Lease Finance and Mitsui, based in Dublin.
markets: Leases engines to airlines and lessors; owners based in the United States and Japan.
rationale: B2B engine lessor with no consumer brand and little marketing need; weak F1 fit overall.
parent: Willis Lease Finance and Mitsui (joint venture)

name: Finnair
desc: Finland's flag-carrier airline, flying from Helsinki to Europe and Asia and listed on Nasdaq Helsinki.
markets: Helsinki hub links Europe with Asia, North America and the Middle East; Finnish state majority owner.
rationale: Nordic flag carrier with Asia network; Nordic and Asian business travellers fit F1 hospitality, but marketing budget is modest.

name: AirAsia
desc: Malaysian low-cost airline brand founded in 2001 by Tony Fernandes, flying across Asia as part of the Capital A group.
markets: Low-cost network across South-East Asia and wider Asia with affiliates in several countries.
rationale: Consumer budget brand with strong marketing history in motorsport; F1 fits Asian growth and brand visibility.

name: Jazeera Airways
desc: Kuwaiti low-cost airline flying scheduled routes from Kuwait to the Middle East, Asia and Europe using Airbus jets.
markets: Kuwait-based network across the Gulf, wider Middle East, South Asia and some European destinations.
rationale: Gulf low-cost carrier with regional consumer reach; Gulf Grand Prix proximity helps, but budget model limits spend.

name: LanzaJet
desc: Produces sustainable aviation fuel using ethanol-to-jet technology licensed to producers and its own plant in Georgia.
markets: US-based fuel producer and technology licensor; planned projects elsewhere are not confirmed here.
rationale: Technology showcase for sustainable fuels in line with F1's fuel goals, but small and early-stage.

name: Strickland Brothers 10 Minute Oil Change
desc: Operates drive-in quick oil change and light maintenance service centres for motorists in the United States.
markets: US consumer chain; locations believed to be in a few US states; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Local consumer service chain; automotive link exists, but regional scale and no international plans limit F1 fit.

name: Cathay Pacific Airways
desc: Hong Kong's flagship airline, flying to more than 80 destinations from its Hong Kong International Airport hub.
markets: Hong Kong hub network across Asia, North America, Europe, Australia and the Middle East.
rationale: Premium Asian carrier with global network and wealthy travellers; rivals Singapore Airlines and Qatar Airways sponsor F1.

name: Zero Gravity Aircraft Industry
desc: Chinese aircraft developer engaged in research and development of aviation vehicles for air transportation and industrial technology.
markets: Appears to be an early-stage Chinese developer; customers and international plans are not confirmed.
rationale: Early-stage Chinese developer with unknown product and no visible brand or marketing activity; weak F1 fit.

name: Sichuan Airlines
desc: Chinese airline based in Chengdu operating an all-Airbus fleet of more than 150 aircraft on domestic and international routes.
markets: Domestic Chinese network plus routes to Asia, Europe and Australia from Chengdu.
rationale: Regional Chinese carrier with consumer reach in western China; F1 helps but spend is likely restrained.

name: Infratil
desc: New Zealand infrastructure investor managed by Morrison & Co, with holdings including CDC Data Centres, Longroad Energy and Qscan.
markets: Holdings in New Zealand, Australia, the United Kingdom and the United States across digital, renewable energy and healthcare assets.
rationale: Investor with little consumer brand; F1 hospitality could suit data-centre and telecom holdings, but fit is indirect.

name: AS Mileage Plan
desc: Financing entity linked to the Alaska Airlines Mileage Plan loyalty programme, used in a loan structure by Alaska Air Group.
markets: Financing structure tied to a US airline loyalty scheme; no separate operations.
rationale: Financing vehicle rather than an operating brand, so no marketing case for an F1 partnership.

name: FLYR
desc: Provides AI-based revenue management, pricing and passenger service systems for airlines.
markets: Sells software to airlines; US headquarters, customer locations not confirmed here.
rationale: Enterprise software vendor with airline customers; F1 hospitality could help sales, but marketing profile is small.

name: Philippine Airlines
desc: Flag carrier of the Philippines and Asia's oldest commercial airline, founded in 1941, flying domestic and international routes.
markets: Manila hub network across the Philippines, Asia, Australia, the Middle East and North America.
rationale: National carrier with large diaspora market; F1 gives regional visibility but spend is modest.

name: Turkish Airlines
desc: Turkish national flag carrier flying from Istanbul to more than 340 destinations in over 130 countries.
markets: Istanbul hub serves Europe, Asia, Africa, North and South America and the Middle East.
rationale: Global flag carrier with heavy sports marketing and Istanbul hub; rivals Qatar and Etihad sponsor F1.

name: Air Europa
desc: Spanish airline based on Mallorca with its main hub in Madrid, flying domestic, European and Latin American routes.
markets: Madrid hub network across Spain, Europe and Latin America and the United States.
rationale: Spanish carrier with Latin American routes and Spanish Grand Prix relevance; fit is plausible but budget is moderate.

name: Breeze Airways
desc: Low-fare US airline founded by JetBlue founder David Neeleman, flying point-to-point routes between secondary US cities.
markets: US point-to-point network between secondary cities, with some Caribbean routes.
rationale: Young low-fare US carrier with a limited marketing budget and domestic focus; weak F1 fit.

name: flynas
desc: Saudi low-cost airline founded in 2007 as Nas Air, flying domestic and international routes from Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam.
markets: Saudi domestic network plus routes to the Middle East, Europe, Asia and Africa.
rationale: Saudi low-cost carrier with Saudi Grand Prix home-market relevance; budget model limits spend.

name: T'way Air
desc: South Korean low-cost airline based in Seoul operating domestic and international flights, mostly to Japan and other Asian destinations.
markets: Low-cost routes from South Korea across Japan, China and South-East Asia.
rationale: Korean budget carrier with Asian consumer reach; F1 fit is modest given price-led brand and limited budget.

name: Akasa Air
desc: Indian low-cost airline based in Mumbai, launched in August 2022 with backing from investor Rakesh Jhunjhunwala.
markets: Indian domestic network plus a few Gulf destinations; young carrier still building its fleet.
rationale: Fast-growing Indian carrier building brand; India's rising F1 interest helps, but budget is limited.

name: easyJet
desc: British low-cost airline founded in 1995 and based at London Luton, flying passengers across Europe and neighbouring regions.
markets: Network of airports across Europe, the UK and North Africa; also sells holidays.
rationale: Large European consumer airline with British Grand Prix relevance; budget brand, though holiday arm adds consumer reach.

name: China Southern Airlines
desc: One of China's three largest state-owned airlines, based in Guangzhou, flying domestic and international routes with hundreds of aircraft.
markets: Domestic Chinese network plus routes to Asia, Europe, North America, Australia and Africa.
rationale: Largest Chinese airline by fleet with global network; Chinese Grand Prix and rival carriers sponsoring F1 support a fit.

name: Wizz Air
desc: Hungarian ultra-low-cost airline founded in 2003, flying a fleet of Airbus aircraft across Europe and to neighbouring countries.
markets: Network across Central and Eastern Europe, Western Europe and nearby Middle East and North Africa destinations.
rationale: European budget airline with young audience and Hungarian Grand Prix home race; brand is price-led.

name: Office National des Aéroports
desc: Morocco's state-owned national airports authority, managing 19 or more civil airports.
markets: Operates airports in Morocco serving domestic and international airlines.
rationale: State airports body with no consumer brand; limited marketing need and weak F1 fit.

name: Saudi Ground Services
desc: Saudi Arabian ground handling provider offering aircraft handling, cargo, passenger services and related airport services.
markets: Operates at Saudi airports; majority owned by the Saudia Group.
rationale: B2B airport service provider; Saudi Grand Prix proximity helps client hospitality, but brand marketing is limited.

name: Avelo Airlines
desc: US low-cost airline based in Houston, launched in 2021, flying Boeing 737 and Embraer jets from secondary airports.
markets: US point-to-point routes plus some Mexico and Caribbean destinations from secondary airports.
rationale: Young low-fare US carrier with a limited marketing budget and domestic focus; weak F1 fit.

name: XCF Global
desc: Produces sustainable aviation fuel and renewable diesel at its Reno, Nevada facility.
markets: Single US production site in Reno supplying fuel markets in North America.
rationale: Young sustainable-fuel producer; F1's sustainable fuel agenda gives a story, but company is small and early.

name: AGS Airports
desc: Owns and operates Aberdeen, Glasgow and Southampton airports in the United Kingdom, earning from airline charges, retail and parking.
markets: Three UK airports serving routes to Europe, North America and domestic destinations.
rationale: Regional airport group with local focus; British Grand Prix proximity is limited, so fit is weak.

name: Cebu Pacific
desc: Philippines' largest low-cost airline, operated by Cebu Air and flying domestic and international routes across Asia.
markets: Philippine domestic network plus routes across Asia, the Middle East and Australia.
rationale: Large Philippine consumer airline with mass-market focus; limited premium angle for F1 and modest budget.

name: Royal Jordanian Airlines
desc: Flag carrier of Jordan, based in Amman and founded in 1963 as Alia, flying from Queen Alia International Airport.
markets: Amman hub network linking the Middle East with Europe, North America and Asia; oneworld member.
rationale: National carrier with Gulf and Levant reach; Abu Dhabi and Saudi races add context, but budget is limited.

name: El Al Israel Airlines
desc: Flag carrier of Israel, based at Ben Gurion Airport and flying to Europe, North America and Asia.
markets: Tel Aviv hub network to Europe, North America and Asia.
rationale: National carrier with international routes; F1 exposure helps but sensitive political context limits partnership use.

name: Scandinavian Airlines
desc: Flag carrier of Denmark, Norway and Sweden, based near Stockholm and a member of the SkyTeam alliance.
markets: Nordic hub network with routes across Europe, North America and Asia.
rationale: Nordic carrier with premium business travellers; F1 hospitality could work, but it recently restructured.
changed: Went through Chapter 11 restructuring in 2022-2024 and was delisted

name: Malaysia Airlines
desc: Malaysia's flag carrier, based at Kuala Lumpur International Airport and part of Malaysia Aviation Group.
markets: Kuala Lumpur hub network across Asia, Australia, the Middle East and Europe.
rationale: Flag carrier from a former Grand Prix host with Asian reach; F1 could rebuild brand visibility.

name: Gogo
desc: Provides inflight internet and connectivity for business aviation aircraft, including air-to-ground and satellite services.
markets: Business jet operators in North America and abroad buy equipment and connectivity services; sold its commercial airline unit in 2020.
rationale: B2B connectivity for business aviation, a premium audience that overlaps F1 hospitality; technology tie-in possible.
changed: Sold its commercial aviation business to Intelsat in 2020

name: Aireon
desc: Provides global space-based air traffic surveillance using ADS-B receivers hosted on Iridium satellites.
markets: Sells surveillance data to air navigation service providers across several world regions.
rationale: Specialist B2B aviation data provider with no consumer profile; weak F1 fit.

name: Toscana Aeroporti
desc: Operates Florence and Pisa airports in Tuscany, Italy, managing passenger services, retail and aviation operations.
markets: Two Tuscan airports serving mainly European holiday and business traffic.
rationale: Regional Italian airport operator; Italian Grand Prix brand link is weak and marketing budget small.

name: Fetcherr
desc: Provides an AI system that optimises airline pricing and revenue management in real time.
markets: Sells AI pricing software to airlines in several regions, including Virgin Atlantic and WestJet.
rationale: Fast-growing B2B AI vendor; F1 gives technology showcase and airline-client hospitality, though marketing budget is moderate.

name: Sun Country Airlines
desc: Leisure and charter airline flying scheduled low-fare service from Minneapolis-St. Paul plus charter and cargo flights.
markets: US network plus Mexico, Caribbean and Central America leisure destinations and charter work.
rationale: Mid-size US leisure carrier with limited marketing budget and a mostly domestic audience; weak F1 fit.
changed: Merger with Allegiant Travel agreed in 2026

name: Jet Airways
desc: Former Indian full-service airline that ceased operations in 2019 and was later ordered into liquidation.
markets: Once flew across India and abroad; no flights since April 2019.
rationale: Defunct airline with no operations since 2019 and no marketing activity; not a sponsorship prospect for F1.
changed: Ceased flying in 2019 and liquidation was ordered in 2024

name: MNG Airlines
desc: Turkish cargo airline of MNG Holding, founded in 1996, flying freighters and some passenger charters.
markets: Cargo flights from Istanbul across Europe, Asia and Africa; belongs to MNG Holding.
rationale: B2B air freight carrier; logistics rivals sponsor F1 but its brand is low-profile, so fit is modest.

name: DFDS
desc: Danish shipping and logistics company, founded in 1866, operating ferries, passenger routes and freight services in Europe.
markets: Ferry and freight routes across Northern Europe, the Mediterranean and the English Channel.
rationale: European ferry and freight brand with consumer and B2B customers; F1 hospitality could help, but marketing needs are regional.

name: Tunisair
desc: National flag-carrier airline of Tunisia, based in Tunis, operating scheduled and charter passenger and cargo flights.
markets: Network linking Tunisia with Europe, North Africa and the Middle East; state majority-owned.
rationale: Financially stretched state carrier with a limited marketing budget and a regional audience; weak F1 fit.

name: PLAY
desc: Former Icelandic low-cost airline that flew transatlantic and European routes from Keflavik until it ceased operations in 2025.
markets: Flew between Iceland, Europe and North America from 2021 until it shut in 2025.
rationale: Defunct airline that stopped operating in 2025 and has no marketing activity; not a sponsorship prospect for F1.
changed: Ceased operations in September 2025

name: Fly Leasing
desc: Irish aircraft lessor owning around 100 aircraft leased to airlines worldwide before being acquired by Carlyle Aviation Partners.
markets: Leased narrowbody and widebody jets to airlines worldwide; now part of Carlyle Aviation Partners.
rationale: B2B lessor without consumer brand; parent Carlyle already sponsors F1, but this unit has little marketing need.
changed: Acquired by Carlyle Aviation Partners in 2021
f1: Parent Carlyle Aviation Partners belongs to Carlyle, a current Formula 1 global partner

name: Alliance Aviation Services
desc: Australian charter and wet-lease airline based in Brisbane flying aircraft for mining, resources and airline customers.
markets: Operates mainly within Australia, with some wet-lease flying for other airlines.
rationale: B2B charter operator for resources clients; low marketing profile and weak F1 fit.

name: Jeju Air
desc: South Korean low-cost airline based in Seoul and Jeju, flying domestic and international routes within Asia.
markets: Korean domestic routes plus Japan, China and South-East Asia destinations.
rationale: Korean budget carrier recovering from a major 2024 crash; limited budget and low premium appeal.

name: South African Airways
desc: South Africa's state-owned flag carrier, based in Johannesburg and a member of Star Alliance, relaunched after business rescue.
markets: Johannesburg hub network across southern and central Africa plus a few intercontinental routes.
rationale: State carrier recovering from restructuring with limited marketing budget; weak F1 fit.
changed: Entered business rescue in 2019

name: LifeMiles
desc: Frequent flyer programme linked to Avianca, letting members earn and redeem miles for flights and partner rewards.
markets: Members across Latin America earn miles from flights, credit cards and partners, then redeem on Avianca and Star Alliance airlines.
rationale: Loyalty brand selling miles to banks and retailers; F1 could add prize experiences, but limited consumer marketing.
